findings.edge1_completeness: Writer completeness is bounded by three censuses: (a) the whole timer cluster 0x5ce0000..0x5cf8000 contains exactly three byte-sized stores to [reg+0x30] from a non-stack base - lock-acquire cmpxchg sites at 0x5cf4842/0x5cf48d7/0x5cf4a52 in body 0x5cf47f0, whose base is a first-argument object with map fields at +0xc0/+0xc8 and a refcount at +0xf8 (lock dec [r14+0xf8]), a shape no wheel has: traced wheel fields end at +0x30 and wheel bases always derive from a handle+selector field or the +0x50 sub-object base; (b) the direct callers of every wheel body (bucket 2, insert 1, setter 2, poll 0 direct / slot 0x64dfe40 only, advance 2) are fully enumerated; (c) the flag writer, advance and poll have no RELATIVE references except poll's single table slot.  A writer that reaches the byte only through a computed pointer or a bulk copy over the whole wheel struct is outside these censuses and is recorded as a boundary, not a finding.
findings.edge1_flag_callers: The flag writer has exactly two direct callers and no RELATIVE references: 0x5ceb47e in body 0x5ceb330 (506 B), which calls it under the wheel lock byte (lock cmpxchg [r15+0x50] at 0x5ceb468) after a refcounted registry-removal phase, passing &[obj+0x10] and ctx+0x150; and 0x5cfc20d in body 0x5cfbfd0 (718 B), a state-machine step that calls it when the task state dword != 3, after draining its queue.  Both are handle/task teardown paths: the flag means "this timer driver is closed", set at teardown, after which the setter can no longer take its direct-store arm.
findings.edge1_flag_writer: The wheel flag byte at [wheel+0x30] (read by the setter at 0x5cea881) is written by exactly one traced body: 0x5ce08e0.  Its argument rsi is the driver sub-object base; it loads the byte at [rsi+0x80] (0x5ce0926) and, only when it is 0, xchg-stores 1 there at 0x5ce093d - [rsi+0x80] is [wheel+0x30] for wheel = [rsi+0x50], the same base it forms at 0x5ce0934 (lea rax,[rsi+0x50]) to call the advance body 0x5ceaa20 at 0x5ce0950 with target u64::MAX, firing every pending entry.  Before the store it asserts dword [rsi+0x90] != 1_000_000_000 through the shared assert callee (slot 0x64df770) with the Location static 0x64c6fa8 (tokio runtime/time/mod.rs, line 190, col 32) and the timers-disabled message. If the byte is already nonzero it returns without storing or advancing: the write is the 0->1 shutdown transition, taken once.
findings.edge1_horizon_writer: The horizon field [wheel+0x28] the insert linked arm compares against has exactly one writer in the traced set: the advance body 0x5ceaa20 stores it at 0x5ceabc4, on its no-more-due arm, with the value derived from the next-deadline body 0x5cf6390 (result at [rsp+0x28]: cmp 1 / adc 0, forced to 0 when the arm flag byte [rsp+0x10] is 0).  The advance body never accesses [wheel+0x30] at all.
findings.edge2_handle_pair: BOUNDED NEGATIVE.  The stored (sec, nsec) pair at [handle+sel+0x88]/[handle+sel+0x90] is only ever loaded in the traced set: the builder 0x5cf2150 (timers-enabled assert), the conversion 0x5cead40 (two asserts and the difference against the deadline), its twin 0x5ceae80 (loads at 0x5ceae9d/0x5ceaecf and a second assert), the flag writer 0x5ce08e0 (cmp at 0x5ce091a) and the two handle drop bodies 0x5ce7f40/0x5cea100 (cmp [obj+0x90] vs 1e9 before freeing the 0x1860-byte levels array).  No body in the chain, its callers or its callees stores to either field from a handle base.  The pair is the runtime clock epoch the handle was built with: runtime data, written by runtime construction outside the traced chain.
findings.edge2_tls_cell: BOUNDED NEGATIVE.  The accessor 0x5cf2b50 reads the thread-local cell at fs:-0x1130 (anchor loaded at 0x5cf2b5a): counter at +0x0, tag at +0x8, handle pointer at +0x10 (0x5cf2be7, then lock xadd +1 on the handle's first word at 0x5cf2bf6), init-state byte at +0x48 (0x5cf2b61).  The PT_TLS template (filesz 0xb20, memsz 0x1180) initialises the cell to {counter 0, tag 2, handle 0, state 0} - tag 2 is the no-live-context state the accessor's reset arm handles.  The only other traced body that writes the cell is its destructor 0x5cdf410, registered through the guard slot 0x64e0510 -> 0x5ca0d20: it stores state byte 2 at 0x5cdf411 and drops the old handle.  A live handle pointer is installed by runtime context entry code that no traced body calls.
findings.edge4_record_1d8: [record+0x1d8] - the &[record+0x150] checker_a instance's sub-state byte [arg+0x88] - has no store anywhere in gate_c (access census over the whole gate body), and before the first funnel call its value is never read: checker_a entry dispatch reads only [arg+0x90], the byte the gate just zeroed; [arg+0x88] is read only on the state-3 re-dispatch, which the zeroed entry byte makes unreachable on a first call, and by the gate only after the call returns.  Its writers are checker_a itself (every fresh-arm outcome that can be observed later writes it) and driver_c's big-endian block copy at 0x2cdf724 (one of four bswap qword stores to record+0x1c0..0x1e0 in a later phase).  The pre-first-call contents are construction leftovers in the driver task object and are functionally dead.
findings.edge4_reinvokers: The gates' only direct re-invokers are two driver bodies: gate_c is called only from driver_c 0x2cde430 (0x2cde6f4 with record mode byte 2, 0x2cdf58b with mode byte 1; in both cases rdi = &[r13+0x220], a record sub-struct of the driver task object, refilled from the driver's own fields before the call), and gate_a only from driver_a 0x2ae41e0 (0x2ae4627 / 0x2ae548c, same shape).  Neither gate nor driver has any RELATIVE reference.  Both drivers are called by one dispatcher body 0x2ae1690 (driver_a at 0x2ae1a47, driver_c at 0x2ae1eeb; driver_a also from 0x2b404b0), and the dispatcher's only direct caller is the stack-context thunk 0x2cd8370 at 0x2cd83a2.
findings.edge4_state3_is_output: Through the gate path, checker state 3 is never a resumed input: gate_c zeroes the checker_a instance state byte [record+0x1e0] at 0x2cbb701 immediately before the funnel call at 0x2cbb717, zeroes the r14-phase instance byte [rbx+0x168] at 0x2cb9914 before the call at 0x2cb9923, and zeroes checker_b's dispatch byte [record+0x1c8] at 0x2cbb476 before the call at 0x2cbb490; gate_a mirrors this.  The same zero-before-call holds at driver_c's own direct checker_a call ([r13+0x2c8] := 0 at 0x2cdfe3a, call at 0x2cdfe4f on &[r13+0x238]) and at the other censused checker_a callers (0x2cc0592, 0x2cc6c9e).  State 3 is written by the checkers during a call (checker_a: [arg+0x88] := 3 and [arg+0x90] := 3 on the predicate-nonzero arm) and consumed by the callers after it: gate_c tests [record+0x1e0] == 3 at 0x2cbb724, and caller 0x2b905a0 tests [rbx+0x180] == 3 at 0x2b90b12 right after its call at 0x2b90b05.

open_edges: Two checker_a call windows (0x2b90b05 in body 0x2b905a0, whose zero store to [rbx+0x180] sits at 0x2b90ddb with untraced ordering, and 0x2cc7fb5 in body 0x2cc1120) and the gate_a-clone callers were not traced far enough to confirm the zero-before-call store; the checker resume arm's reachability through those callers stays open.

The stack-context thunk 0x2cd8370 has no direct caller and no RELATIVE reference in the artifact; the mechanism that invokes it (and thus how often the dispatcher re-invokes the drivers) is outside the two censused reference forms.
A writer of the wheel flag byte that works only through a computed pointer or a bulk copy over the whole wheel struct would be invisible to this packet's censuses (see edge1_completeness).

The two carried edges of the bucket-second-caller packet (#2701) - the owning object of the 0x64dfe40 method table and the wheel list's poll-side consumer - are different objects from this packet's three edges and are NOT folded in; the advance body was checked and does not touch the wheel list head/tail fields [wheel+0x18] / [wheel+0x20] (its list-shaped accesses are on entry fields), so it is not that consumer either.
